analysis.title: Russell 2k Futures: Buying The Rate Driven Reversal?
key_insights: Russell 2000 fell -4.2% from Sept 1-30, lagging Nasdaq (+4.6%) and S&P (unchanged). GS attributes the lag to rate market dynamics: an incrementally hawkish Fed priced more hikes, and higher oil and competition for capital pushed real rates up along the curve.

Funding spreads richened despite the underperformance. Russell 2k 3-month funding versus Fed Funds rose +9bps, and the Russell 2k discount to S&P funding narrowed to its tightest since early February before reverting slightly.

Commitment of Traders data for Sept 1-22 shows contrarian buying by professional investors. Non-Dealers bought +$3bn of Russell 2k futures, led by Asset Managers (+$2.2bn), with Hedge Funds (+$200mm) and Non-Reportables (+$560mm).
Non-Dealer net positioning was at a multiyear minimum on Sept 1, so GS suggests the buying may reflect a starting point for positioning that was simply too low.

GS offers a counterpoint: incremental support may wane as credit deteriorates. CDX High Yield closed Sept 30 at roughly a 5-month maximum, and weekly changes in Asset Manager shorts and CDX HY have historically been positively correlated.

tension_points.bull_case: Professional investors bought +$3bn of Russell 2k futures from Sept 1-22 from a multiyear-low positioning base, funding spreads richened, and the discount to S&P funding narrowed to its tightest since early February.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit is deteriorating, with CDX High Yield at an approximate 5-month max on Sept 30, and Asset Manager shorts have historically moved with CDX HY, so incremental support may wane.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued CDX High Yield widening beyond the approximate 5-month high would undercut the contrarian-flow thesis.
